steps.analyst_reply: {"root_cause": "The scorecard runs on a single holistic feature, and it fails in two systematic ways: it treats any occurrence of 'surgery' as surgeon evidence (refractive surgery/LASIK ophthalmologists, a 'Department of Surgery' mailing address, NP/PA-style profiles that 'specialize in Orthopaedic Surgery'), and it misses real surgeons whose boilerplate bios never say 'surgeon' but name an orthopedic practice, a surgical group, sports medicine, or joint replacement (Ocean Orthopedic Associates, Seton Surgical Group, Hospital for Special Surgery). The labeled sample confirms both regularities: ophthalmology and Ms./Mr.-titled profiles are consistently physician, while orthopedics/sports-medicine/surgical-group affiliations are consistently surgeon. Targeted specialty and credential elements supply the discriminative features the holistic answer cannot express; the remaining signal-free disagreements are irreducible from text.", "add_elements": [{"key": "surgical_specialty_mention", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the text connect this person to a surgical specialty \u2014 such as orthopedic surgery, neurosurgery, plastic or cosmetic surgery, general surgery, trauma or hand surgery, surgical oncology, or joint replacement \u2014 or to a practice, hospital, or institute whose name contains 'surgery', 'surgical', or 'orthopedic'?", "criteria": null}, {"key": "eye_care_ophthalmology", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Is this person's practice focused on the eye or vision \u2014 for example ophthalmology, LASIK, refractive or vision-correction surgery, cataracts, cornea, retina, or glaucoma?", "criteria": null}, {"key": "non_doctor_title_or_app", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Is this person referred to with a courtesy title such as Ms., Miss, Mrs., Mr., or Mx. rather than Dr., or described as an advanced practice provider (APP), nurse practitioner, or physician assistant?", "criteria": null}], "retire_elements": [], "reword_elements": []}
